title: 2012 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement:
Paula the painter and her two helpers each paint at constant, but different, rates. They always start at \(8:00\) AM, and all three always take the same amount of time to eat lunch.

On Monday the three of them painted \(50\%\) of a house, quitting at \(4:00\) PM. On Tuesday, when Paula wasn’t there, the two helpers painted only \(24\%\) of the house and quit at \(2:12\) PM. On Wednesday Paula worked by herself and finished the house by working until \(7:12\) P.M.

How long, in minutes, was each day’s lunch break?

solutions.text:
Let the lunch break be \(m\) minutes, Paula’s rate be \(p\) percent per minute, and the helpers’ combined rate be \(h\) percent per minute.

Monday gives \((p+h)(480-m)=50\). Tuesday gives \(h(372-m)=24\). Since the remaining work on Wednesday was \(26\) percent, Wednesday gives \(p(672-m)=26\).

Adding the Tuesday and Wednesday equations and subtracting the Monday equation gives \(108h-192p=0\), so \(h=\dfrac{16}{9}p\).

Substituting into Monday gives \(\dfrac{25}{9}p(480-m)=50\), while Wednesday gives \(p(672-m)=26\). Solving these two equations gives \(m=48\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Let the lunch break be \(m\) minutes
Use Monday for \(p+h\), Tuesday for \(h\), and Wednesday for \(p\)
